# Improving the Writing Process {.unnumbered}

Writing is a crucial part of the scientific process. It is important to communicate your findings clearly and effectively. 
However, refining your text can be difficult, especially without external feedback.
For this, LLMs can help in providing fast feedback and suggestions for improvement.
In addition, LLM tools can also help you to improve your writing by providing suggestions for better phrasing, grammar, and style.

However, it is important to keep in mind that LLMs can also introduce errors and biases into your writing. 
For example, they tend to be overly positive and may not catch all mistakes.
Thus, all the reviews and suggestions should be carefully checked and verified.

## Grammar and Style Checking

For grammar and style checking, we often use [Grammarly](https://www.grammarly.com/).
It can be used as a browser extension or as a standalone application.
It provides suggestions for improving grammar, spelling, and style.
We find this app very useful for quickly pointing to grammar mistakes and typos.

## Feedback for Improving Text

For more general feedback on how to improve a text, we often use [ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/) or other web-based LLMs such as [DeepSeek](https://chat.deepseek.com/).
However, each model has its own style and biases, so it is important to experiment with different models to find the one that works best for you.

In general we use LLMs to provide feedback on how to improve the text, e.g. by making it more concise, clearer, or more engaging.

### Example: Making the text less positive

Here we asked ChatGPT for feedback on the current text, and if it is already neutral enough.
The example text is from the [LLMs as Optimizers](06-accelerating_applications.qmd#sec-llm-optimizers) section.
We simply use a prompt like the following:

```markdown
From the next text, I got some reviews saying that the text read positively. I have made some changes, and now it should read less positively, and only as a potential promise of LLMs solving stuff, is it enough? 
Do not write new text, but detail the flaws and the overly positive text pointing to the sentences that need to be change.

Text:

\subsection{LLMs as Optimizers} \label{sec:llm-optimizers} 


Discovering novel compounds and reactions in chemistry and materials science has long...
```

The response we got was the following (shortened for clarity):

```markdown
Got it—here’s a focused pass flagging language that still reads as overly positive or promise-like, with why it’s an issue and what to adjust (without rewriting). I’ve grouped them by section and quoted the exact spans that should be toned down.

# LLMs as Optimizers (intro)

* “**Recent advances in LLMs have unlocked potential for targeting optimization challenges…**”
  *Issue:* Hype-y “unlocked potential.”
  *Adjust:* Neutralize (“have been explored for…”) and add scope/conditions.

* “**A key strength of LLMs lies in their capacity to frame optimization tasks through natural language, which potentially can enhance…**”
  *Issue:* “Key strength” + implied general enhancement.
  *Adjust:* Recast as a hypothesis/possibility and specify when/where this was shown.

... [similar points omitted for brevity] ...

If you address the quoted spans above—mainly by hedging, attributing strictly to specific studies/benchmarks, and removing intensifiers—you’ll land a clearly “potential” framing without reading as optimistic marketing.
```

Using the feedback, and iterating several times, one can improve the text to be more neutral, without waiting for other people to review it.

### Example 2: Making the text more smooth

Another example that we use a lot is to make the text more smooth and easier to read. 
In this case, we focus especially on transitions between sentences and paragraphs.

For this, we use a similar prompt as the previous one:

```markdown
I am writing a scientific article. Can you help me improve the readability of the following text?

Please focus especially on transitions between sentences and paragraphs. Or if something reads strange, please point it out.

Here is the text:

{text}
```

The response of the model will be a point-by-point review of the text, often already including some suggestions for improvement.

## Guidelines

- [ ] (Recommended) Use Grammarly or similar tools to catch grammar mistakes and typos while writing
- [ ] Use LLMs to get fast feedback on your writing after you have written a first draft
- [ ] Always carefully check the suggestions and reviews
- [ ] Experiment with different LLMs to find the one that works best for you
- [ ] Use LLMs to make the text more neutral and less biased
- [ ] Use LLMs to make the text more engaging and interesting to read
- [ ] ALWAYS ensure that the final text is YOUR text and YOUR message
- [ ] Do not rely solely on LLMs for writing, always seek feedback from humans as well
